title: Quiet the Mind
description: Racing thoughts, overthinking and a brain that won't switch off at bedtime. Practical, calm ways to settle a busy mind before sleep.
intro: If your body is tired but your head is still running through the day, tomorrow's list or an old conversation, you are in the right place. These guides explain why minds get busier at night and walk through practical ways to settle them, from worry lists and breathing to simple changes in the hour before bed.

title: Falling Asleep
description: Why it can take so long to drop off, and what genuinely helps: bedtime routines, wind-down habits and what to do when sleep won't come.
intro: Lying awake waiting for sleep is frustrating, and the frustration itself makes it harder. These guides cover how long falling asleep should normally take, why it sometimes takes far longer, and the routines and techniques that give sleep the best chance of arriving on its own.

title: Waking at Night
description: Waking at 3am, waking too early, or lying awake unable to get back to sleep. Understand why it happens and how to settle back down.
intro: Brief wakings are a normal part of sleep. The problem starts when a wake-up turns into an hour of staring at the ceiling. These guides explain what is going on when you wake in the night, when it is worth speaking to a GP, and the calm, practical steps that make it easier to drift back off.

title: Sleep Sounds
description: Brown noise, white noise, pink noise, rain and nature sounds. What each one is, what the evidence says, and how to use sound for sleep.
intro: Sound can mask the noises that wake you and give a restless mind something steady to settle on. These guides explain the differences between brown, white and pink noise, what rain and nature sounds offer, and how to use sound at night without it becoming a crutch.

title: Sleep Environment
description: Temperature, darkness, noise, light and bedding. How to set up a bedroom that makes good sleep easier, with UK homes in mind.
intro: Your bedroom is doing more work than you might think. Light, noise, temperature and clutter all shape how easily you fall asleep and how often you wake. These guides cover the changes that make the biggest difference, most of them cheap or free.

title: Relaxation
description: Breathing exercises, progressive muscle relaxation, body scans and bedtime meditation. Techniques you can learn in an evening.
intro: Relaxation techniques give a wired body and mind a clear, simple task to do instead of trying to force sleep. These step-by-step guides cover the methods with the best track record, how to practise them, and how to fit them into a bedtime routine.

title: Sleep Habits
description: Sleep hygiene, screens, caffeine, alcohol, exercise and keeping a consistent schedule. Daily habits that add up to better nights.
intro: What you do during the day and in the hours before bed shapes the night ahead. These guides look at the everyday habits with the strongest links to sleep, explain what the evidence actually says, and suggest realistic changes rather than rules nobody keeps.

title: Sleep Products
description: Plain-English buying guides for sleep masks, earplugs, white noise machines, sleep headphones, pillows, blackout curtains and more.
intro: Most sleep problems are not solved by buying something. But a few well-chosen products genuinely make a dark, quiet, comfortable bedroom easier to achieve. These guides explain what to look for, what the trade-offs are, and where products are worth considering. Where we link to a product, it is clearly marked and we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.

title: Sleep Questions
description: Straight answers to common sleep questions: why can't I sleep, how much sleep do adults need, can you catch up on sleep, and when to see a GP.
intro: Short, direct answers to the questions people ask most about sleep, with links to deeper guides where you want more. If a sleep problem is persistent or affecting your health, we also explain when it is worth talking to a GP.
